cards.p: Carbon monoxide (CO) is a colorless, odorless gas that comes from badly burning stoves or water heaters. It binds to hemoglobin about 200 times more tightly than O2. So the blood cannot carry O2.

once.soru: A badly burning stove is in a closed room. Everyone has a headache. What should be done first?

secenekler.neden: In CO poisoning, the first step is to ventilate. Then oxygen is given and medical help is called.
While asleep you keep breathing in CO, which is very dangerous.
A painkiller does not remove CO from the blood.

cards.p: The breathing rhythm is set by the medulla in the brainstem, and the pons fine-tunes it. The strongest trigger for breathing is a rise in CO2 in the blood. When CO2 rises, the pH drops, and breathing gets faster and deeper.

cards.p: During exercise, CO2 rises and breathing and heart rate speed up. At high altitude, the air is still 21% O2, but because air pressure is low, PO2 falls. Over time, the number of red blood cells in the blood increases.

cards.p: In asthma the bronchioles narrow, and in bronchitis the bronchi become inflamed. In COPD the airways narrow permanently, and in pneumonia the alveoli fill with fluid. Smoking damages the cilia.

once.soru: Why does a smoker cough in the morning?

secenekler.neden: Because the cilia are damaged, mucus cannot be swept away and builds up. The body removes this mucus by coughing.
Smoking does not make the lungs grow. It damages the airways.
The cough comes from built-up mucus, not from blood.

cards.p: When you run, CO<sub>2</sub> rises and the medulla speeds up breathing. Adrenaline speeds up the heart. When water is lost through sweat, the kidneys hold on to water under the effect of the hormone ADH. The systems keep the internal balance together.

once.soru: Your breathing speeds up when you run. Which system speeds up too?

secenekler.neden: The heart speeds up, and more blood and oxygen go to the muscles.
While running, less blood goes to digestion.
The reproductive system has no such role in exercise.

cards.p:
• The respiratory system exchanges gases, and cellular respiration makes ATP.
• The airways warm, moisten and filter the air.
• When the diaphragm contracts, chest volume increases, pressure drops and air flows in.
• Gases cross by diffusion, driven by partial pressure differences.
• O2 is mostly carried by hemoglobin, and CO2 mostly as bicarbonate.

quiz.q: A person has a tidal volume of 450 mL, an inspiratory reserve volume of 2500 mL, an expiratory reserve volume of 1000 mL and a residual volume of 1200 mL. What is their vital capacity in mL?
quiz.e: Vital capacity is the tidal volume plus the two reserve volumes. 450 + 2500 + 1000 = 3950 mL. Residual air cannot be breathed out, so it is not added to this total.

quiz.q: During an asthma attack, the airway narrows most in the bronchioles. Why?
o: Bronchioles have no cartilage rings.
Bronchioles never secrete mucus.
Bronchiole walls are lined with thick cartilage rings.
Bronchioles exchange gases like alveoli.
quiz.e: Cartilage rings hold the trachea and bronchi open. Bronchioles have no cartilage. In asthma, when the smooth muscle of the bronchiole contracts, the airway narrows easily.
y: More mucus adds to the narrowing. But the main cause is the contraction of smooth muscle in a wall with no cartilage.
It is the opposite, because cartilage keeps the airway open. The bronchiole can narrow because it has no cartilage.
Gas exchange happens in the alveolus. The narrowing of the bronchiole comes from the smooth muscle in its wall.

quiz.q: Put each change that happens at rest under breathing in or breathing out.
quiz.e: When you breathe in, the diaphragm and external intercostal muscles contract. The ribs rise, the volume increases, the pressure drops and air flows in. At rest, breathing out is passive. The muscles relax, the volume decreases and the pressure rises.

quiz.q: At the start of a capillary, PO<sub>2</sub> = 100 and PCO<sub>2</sub> = 40 mmHg. At its end, PO<sub>2</sub> = 40 and PCO<sub>2</sub> = 45 mmHg. Where is this capillary most likely to be?
o: Around an alveolus
In the pulmonary vein
Inside the trachea
In a skeletal muscle
quiz.e: The blood in this capillary has lost O<sub>2</sub> and gained CO<sub>2</sub>. This happens in tissues where O<sub>2</sub> is used. In the alveolus the opposite happens.
y: Around the alveolus, blood takes in O₂ and PO₂ rises. Here PO₂ falls, so this is a tissue capillary.
The pulmonary vein is not a capillary and carries oxygenated blood. A drop in PO₂ shows that O₂ is being given to a tissue.
The trachea is an airway, not a blood capillary. If PO₂ falls and PCO₂ rises, the capillary is in a working tissue.

bosaltim.title: Excretory system
bosaltim.summary: How does the body get rid of waste and keep its internal balance?

cards.p: Metabolism constantly makes waste. This waste is CO2, nitrogenous waste, extra water and salt. Excretion removes this waste and keeps the water, salt and pH balance of the blood. This balance is called homeostasis.

cards.key: Excretion is not just removing waste. Adjusting the makeup of the blood is also its job.

once.soru: When you drink a lot of water, you urinate more. Why does the kidney remove the extra water?

secenekler.neden: The water and salt levels of the blood are kept within narrow limits. Any excess is removed.
Water is not harmful. Only an excess upsets the balance.
The bladder only stores urine. How much water to remove depends on the balance of the blood.

cards.p: When amino acids are broken down, toxic ammonia forms, and a lot of water is needed to dilute it. Living things turn ammonia into less toxic urea or uric acid. This conversion takes energy.

once.soru: When proteins are broken down, which waste forms that does not form from carbohydrates?

secenekler.neden: The amino group in amino acids carries nitrogen. When amino acids are broken down, ammonia forms from this group.
CO₂ and water also form when carbohydrates and fats are broken down. Protein breakdown makes nitrogenous waste on top of these.
Glucose is a fuel, not a waste.

cards.h: Life in water, life on land
cards.p: The type of waste an animal gets rid of depends on how much water it has access to. Most bony fish excrete ammonia, and mammals excrete urea. Birds, most reptiles and insects excrete uric acid.

cards.h: Urea is made in the liver
cards.p: The liver combines ammonia with CO2 and turns it into urea. This process is called the ornithine cycle, and it uses ATP. Urea passes into the blood and is filtered in the kidney. So the kidney does not make urea, it only removes it.

cards.p: The lungs remove CO2 and water vapor, and the skin removes water and salt in sweat. The liver adds pigments to bile. The large intestine removes these pigments and some minerals from the body.

cards.key: Bile pigments come from broken-down red blood cells. Getting rid of undigested food is not excretion, it is defecation.

once.soru: Besides the kidney, which organ also carries out excretion?

secenekler.neden: The lungs remove CO₂ and water vapor from the blood.
The stomach digests food. It does not excrete.
The heart pumps blood. It does not remove waste.

cards.p: Urine forms in the kidney, flows down the ureter to the bladder and collects there. When the bladder is full, urine leaves through the urethra. The internal sphincter is involuntary, and the external sphincter is voluntary.

cards.key: The kidneys sit on either side of the lower back. Two ureters run from the kidneys to the bladder. There is only one urethra leading out of the bladder.

once.soru: You can hold in your urine for a while. What makes this possible?

secenekler.neden: The external sphincter at the bladder's exit is voluntary, and you contract it yourself.
The kidney keeps making urine, and it collects in the bladder.
The ureter carries urine from the kidney to the bladder. The bladder's exit is closed by a sphincter.

cards.p: The outer part of the kidney is called the cortex, and the middle part is the medulla. In the inner part is the renal pelvis, where urine collects. Each kidney has about a million filtering units called nephrons.

cards.key: The glomerulus and Bowman's capsule are in the cortex, and the loop of Henle is in the medulla. Urine leaves the renal pelvis through the ureter.

once.soru: About how many filtering units does one kidney have?

secenekler.neden: Each kidney has about a million nephrons.
The real number is much larger. The kidney filters blood in a very large number of tiny units.
The real number is about a thousand times larger.

cards.h: The nephron: the kidney's filtering unit
cards.p: Blood comes to a ball of capillaries called the glomerulus, and Bowman's capsule collects the filtrate. The filtrate passes through the proximal tubule, the loop of Henle, the distal tubule and the collecting duct, in that order.

cards.key: Many nephrons open into one shared collecting duct. Urine flows from there into the renal pelvis.

etk.soru: Tap the parts of the nephron and follow the path of the filtrate.

noktalar.acik: The glomerulus is a ball of capillaries. The high blood pressure here filters part of the plasma into the capsule.
Bowman's capsule wraps the glomerulus like a cup. It collects the filtrate and sends it into the tubule.
All of the glucose and amino acids, and most of the water and Na<sup>+</sup>, are reabsorbed into the blood here.
The loop of Henle is a U-shaped bend that reaches into the medulla. It helps concentrate the urine by allowing water and salt to be reabsorbed.
Secretion happens in the distal tubule, and Na<sup>+</sup> reabsorption continues under the effect of aldosterone.
The collecting duct is shared by many nephrons. ADH increases water reabsorption here.

once.soru: Where is blood first filtered in the kidney?

secenekler.neden: This ball of capillaries is called the glomerulus. Plasma filters from here into the capsule.
The bladder only stores urine. Filtering happens in the kidney.
The ureter carries finished urine.

cards.p: The high pressure in the glomerulus pushes plasma into the capsule. Water, glucose, amino acids, salt and urea pass into the capsule. Blood cells and large proteins do not. No ATP is used in this filtration.

cards.p: Useful substances return from the tubules to the blood. All of the glucose and amino acids, and most of the water and Na+, are reabsorbed. Most reabsorption happens in the proximal tubule, and about 99% of the filtrate returns to the blood.

cards.p: In secretion, H+, K+, ammonia and some drugs are moved from the blood into the tubule. When the blood becomes acidic, more H+ is secreted. This keeps the blood pH at about 7.4.

cards.h: The loop of Henle and concentrated urine
cards.p: The ascending limb of the loop of Henle releases salt into the medulla, but does not let water through. So the medulla gets saltier the deeper you go. Water leaves the descending limb and the collecting duct by osmosis, and the urine becomes concentrated.

once.soru: The kangaroo rat lives in the desert and almost never drinks water. Which part of its kidney is very long?

secenekler.neden: A long loop of Henle makes the medulla very salty. So water is recovered and the urine is very concentrated.
The ureter only carries urine. It does not recover water.
The bladder stores urine, but it does not set how concentrated the urine is.

cards.p: When you drink little water, the pituitary releases ADH. The collecting duct reabsorbs more water and urine decreases. When blood pressure drops, aldosterone increases Na+ reabsorption in the distal tubule.

cards.h: How does blood change as it passes through the kidney?
cards.p: In the blood leaving the kidney, urea has dropped, and water and salt are balanced. Because kidney cells carry out respiration, O<sub>2</sub> and glucose drop in this blood and CO<sub>2</sub> rises.

once.soru: Compared with the renal artery, what has decreased in the blood of the renal vein?

secenekler.neden: Urea is filtered and removed in the urine.
Kidney cells carry out respiration, so CO₂ increases.
Red blood cells are not filtered, so their number does not change.

cards.p: Drinking too little water can lead to kidney stones. If the kidneys fail, urea and K+ build up in the blood. Then the blood is cleaned by dialysis, or a kidney transplant is done.

once.soru: A dialysis machine passes blood across a semipermeable membrane. What must not cross the membrane?

secenekler.neden: Blood cells and proteins must stay in the blood. That is why the membrane does not let them through.
Urea crosses the membrane, because the goal of dialysis is to remove urea.
Extra salt also crosses the membrane and is removed.

cards.p:
• Excretion keeps the internal balance, that is, homeostasis.
• Ammonia is the main waste in aquatic animals, urea in mammals and uric acid in birds and insects. Urea is made in the liver.
• In the nephron, urine forms through filtration, reabsorption and secretion.
• ADH increases water reabsorption, and aldosterone increases Na+ reabsorption.
• Urine follows the path kidney, ureter, bladder, urethra.

quiz.q: A person forms 180 L of filtrate a day, and 98.5% of the filtrate is reabsorbed. How many liters of urine form per day?
quiz.e: The part not reabsorbed is 1.5%. 180 × 0.015 = 2.7 L. A small drop in the reabsorption percentage greatly increases the amount of urine.

quiz.q: Starting where blood is filtered, put in order the path the filtrate takes through the nephron.
quiz.e: Plasma is filtered from the glomerulus into Bowman's capsule. The filtrate passes through the proximal tubule, the loop of Henle and the distal tubule and opens into the collecting duct. Urine flows from there into the renal pelvis.

quiz.q: Which of these are found in a healthy person's urine? Put each one in the right group.
quiz.e: Urea is filtered and removed. H<sup>+</sup> and ammonia are secreted into the tubule. All of the glucose and amino acids are reabsorbed. Red blood cells and large proteins are never filtered in the glomerulus.

quiz.q: After heavy bleeding, a person's blood pressure drops. What is expected in the kidney?
o: Renin drops and Na⁺ excretion rises.
Renin and aldosterone rise, and Na⁺ and water are reabsorbed.
ADH drops and urine becomes plentiful.
Filtration in the glomerulus speeds up and urine increases.
quiz.e: When blood pressure drops, the kidney releases renin, and at the end of the chain aldosterone rises. Na⁺ is reabsorbed in the distal tubule, and water follows it. This protects blood volume.
y: When pressure drops, the kidney does not lower renin, it raises it. The goal is to keep Na⁺ and water.
After blood loss, ADH rises and water is kept. So urine decreases.
When blood pressure drops, filtration in the glomerulus decreases, not increases.

ureme-sistemi.title: Reproductive system and embryonic development
ureme-sistemi.summary: Learn the reproductive organs, the cycle and how the embryo develops, from gamete formation to birth.

cards.p: Sperm are made in the testes. The testes sit in a pouch that is 2-3 °C cooler than the body. Sperm mature in the epididymis and are carried by the vas deferens. Mixed with gland secretions, they form semen.

cards.p: Sperm are made in the seminiferous tubules. Sertoli cells are stimulated by FSH and nourish the sperm. Leydig cells are stimulated by LH and secrete testosterone.

cards.p: Spermatogonia (2n) multiply by mitosis. A primary spermatocyte undergoes meiosis to form four spermatids (n), which become sperm. Sperm production continues for life from puberty on.

once.soru: How many sperm form when one primary spermatocyte completes meiosis?

secenekler.neden: Meiosis produces four cells, and all four become sperm.
One gamete from one cell happens in oogenesis. In spermatogenesis, all four cells become sperm.
Meiosis has two divisions and ends with four cells.

cards.p: The ovaries produce oocytes and secrete estrogen and progesterone. The oocyte is fertilized in the oviduct, and the embryo develops in the uterus. The vagina is the birth canal.

once.soru: Where does fertilization usually take place?

secenekler.neden: The sperm meets the oocyte in the upper part of the oviduct.
The embryo develops in the uterus. Fertilization happens before that.
The ovary releases the oocyte. Fertilization happens in the oviduct.

cards.p: Oogenesis begins before birth and pauses in meiosis I. After puberty, one oocyte resumes development in each cycle. Meiosis II is completed only if a sperm enters the oocyte.

cards.p: The cycle lasts 28 days on average. During menstruation, the uterine lining is shed, and in the follicular phase it thickens again. At ovulation, around day 14, the oocyte is released. Then the corpus luteum forms.

once.soru: Ovulation happens about 14 days before the next period. On which day is ovulation in a 32-day cycle?

secenekler.neden: Day 14 applies to a 28-day cycle. In a 32-day cycle, ovulation shifts later.
The phase after ovulation always lasts about 14 days. So it is day 32 − 14 = 18.

cards.p: FSH makes the follicle grow, and the follicle secretes estrogen. High estrogen causes a sudden surge in LH, and ovulation occurs. Progesterone from the corpus luteum maintains the uterine lining and suppresses FSH and LH.
cards.key: Estrogen raising LH is positive feedback. Progesterone suppressing FSH and LH is negative feedback. Without fertilization, progesterone falls and menstruation begins.

cards.p: At puberty, estrogen starts the cycle. Between ages 45 and 55, the follicles run out and the cycle stops. This is called menopause. The birth control pill suppresses FSH and LH, so ovulation does not occur.

once.soru: How does the birth control pill prevent ovulation?

secenekler.neden: The hormones in the pill suppress the pituitary, so the follicle does not mature.
The pill does not destroy oocytes. It only stops them from maturing.
The pill works through hormones. It does not close the uterus.

cards.p: The sperm enters the oocyte in the oviduct and a zygote (2n) forms. The zygote divides by mitosis, first into a morula and then into a fluid-filled blastocyst. Around day 6-7 the blastocyst embeds in the uterus. This is called implantation.

cards.p: In the gastrula stage, three germ layers separate. The outer layer is the ectoderm, the middle one the mesoderm and the inner one the endoderm. The neural tube forms from the ectoderm. After week 8, the embryo is called a fetus.

etk.soru: Tap the embryonic membranes and the placenta.

noktalar.acik: The chorion is the outermost membrane and forms the embryo's part of the placenta.
The amnion is a fluid-filled membrane around the embryo. It protects the embryo from bumps and drying out.
The embryo is the new individual that develops as the zygote divides by mitosis.
The umbilical cord connects the embryo to the placenta. Its vessels bring food and oxygen and carry wastes away.
In birds, the allantois stores wastes. In humans, it helps form the umbilical cord vessels.
In birds, the yolk sac provides food. In humans, it makes the first blood cells.
The placenta exchanges substances between mother and baby. The two bloods normally do not mix.

once.soru: How is the baby protected from bumps in the uterus?

secenekler.neden: The fluid inside the amnion cushions bumps.
The baby's bones are still soft. Amniotic fluid provides the protection.
The placenta exchanges substances. Amniotic fluid absorbs the bumps.

cards.p: In the placenta, the mother's blood and the baby's blood do not mix. Oxygen, nutrients and some antibodies pass from mother to baby. CO<sub>2</sub> and urea pass from baby to mother. Blood cells do not cross the placenta.

once.soru: Does nicotine from a pregnant woman's cigarette reach the baby?

secenekler.neden: Nicotine, alcohol and some drugs cross the placenta.
The placenta stops blood cells, but it cannot stop nicotine.
Nicotine reaches the baby every day throughout pregnancy.

cards.p: The embryo that implants in the uterus secretes the hormone hCG. hCG keeps the corpus luteum alive, so menstruation does not occur. Pregnancy tests look for this hormone. During birth, oxytocin makes the uterus contract.

once.soru: Can a girl and a boy be identical twins?

secenekler.neden: Identical twins have the same genes, so they also have the same sex.
Genes determine sex. Twins with the same genes have the same sex.
The time of birth does not change sex.

once.soru: Can HIV infection be treated with antibiotics?

secenekler.neden: HIV is a virus. Antibiotics act only on bacteria.
Antibiotics do not kill viruses.
Antibiotics do not act on viruses at any stage.

cards.p:
• In the testis, Sertoli cells are stimulated by FSH and Leydig cells by LH.
• Oogenesis begins before birth, and meiosis II is completed at fertilization.
• High estrogen raises LH, and LH triggers ovulation.
• The zygote becomes a morula and a blastocyst, implants in the uterus, and then a gastrula forms.
• hCG maintains the corpus luteum, and oxytocin speeds up birth.

quiz.q: At least how many primary spermatocytes must complete meiosis to produce 60 sperm?
quiz.e: Each primary spermatocyte forms 4 spermatids by meiosis, and these become sperm. So 60 ÷ 4 = 15 spermatocytes are needed.

quiz.q: Put the events from fertilization to germ layer formation in order.
ogeler: A sperm enters the secondary oocyte in the oviduct
The nuclei fuse and a zygote (2n) forms
The blastocyst embeds in the uterine lining (implantation)
Three germ layers separate in the gastrula
quiz.e: Fertilization happens in the oviduct and a zygote forms. Dividing by mitosis, the zygote forms first a morula and then a blastocyst. The blastocyst embeds in the uterus on day 6-7. Then the ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm separate in the gastrula.

quiz.q: Match each hormone to its job.
quiz.e: FSH makes the follicle grow, and the LH surge triggers ovulation. Progesterone from the corpus luteum maintains the uterine lining. hCG from the embryo keeps the corpus luteum alive. Oxytocin contracts the uterus at birth.

quiz.q: Which is true for twins where one is a girl and one is a boy?
o: They are identical twins
They are fraternal twins
Their genes are the same, only the sex chromosomes differ
One changed sex after a single zygote split
quiz.e: Identical twins come from the same zygote, so their genes and sex are the same. Twins of different sexes come from two separate zygotes.
y: Identical twins come from the same zygote and are always the same sex. Being born on the same day is not the test.
Twins of different sexes come from two separate zygotes. Their genes differ as much as ordinary siblings' genes do.
Sex is set at fertilization and does not change later. Different sexes show there were two separate zygotes.

ekosistem.title: Ecosystem ecology and current environmental problems
ekosistem.summary: How does energy flow, how does matter cycle, and what disrupts an ecosystem?

cards.p: The interaction of living things (biotic) with the nonliving surroundings (abiotic) such as light, water and soil is called an ecosystem. From smallest to largest, the levels are the individual, the population, the community, the ecosystem and the biosphere.

once.soru: Which level do all the carp in a lake form?

secenekler.neden: The individuals of one species living in an area form a population.
A community includes all the species in the lake.
An ecosystem also includes the nonliving surroundings.

cards.p: The place where an organism lives is called its habitat. A habitat is like the organism's address. An ecological niche is the organism's role in the ecosystem, which is like its job. What an organism eats, when it feeds and which resources it uses determine its niche.

once.soru: Two birds live in the same tree. One eats insects by day, and the other eats fruit at night. What is different about these birds?

secenekler.neden: What they eat and when they feed, in other words their roles, are different.
Both live in the same tree, so they share an address.
They feed in different ways, so their niches are different too.

cards.p: Producers make food from inorganic substances. They do this by photosynthesis or with chemical energy, which is chemosynthesis. Consumers take in ready-made food. Decomposers such as bacteria and fungi break down dead remains and return minerals to the soil.

cards.key: Consumers can be herbivores, carnivores, omnivores or scavengers. Chemosynthetic organisms get energy by oxidizing inorganic substances.

etk.soru: Place each organism by its role in the ecosystem.
ogeler: Cyanobacteria carry out photosynthesis, so they are producers.
It makes food from inorganic substances by chemosynthesis, so it is a producer.
A vulture is a scavenger. It eats dead animals, so it is a consumer. The organisms that break dead remains down all the way to minerals are the decomposers.

once.soru: In a forest, which organisms turn dead leaves into minerals?

secenekler.neden: Decay bacteria and fungi break down dead remains.
Producers make food. They do not break down dead remains.
Scavengers eat dead animals, but the ones that break them down to minerals are the decomposers.

cards.p: A food chain shows how food and energy pass from one organism to the next. Each link in the chain is called a trophic level. When chains connect to each other, they form a food web.

once.soru: In a chain of grass, grasshopper and frog, what do the arrows show?

secenekler.neden: An arrow is drawn from the organism that is eaten to the one that eats it. Energy passes in that direction too.
The arrow is drawn from the eaten to the eater, not from predator to prey.
The arrows have nothing to do with the size of the organisms.

cards.p: Energy enters an ecosystem as sunlight. At each level, most of the energy is lost as heat through respiration. Only about 10% passes to the next level up. So energy flows in one direction, while matter cycles.

cards.p: Matter moves through an ecosystem in cycles. The water cycle runs through evaporation, transpiration from leaves, condensation and precipitation. In the carbon cycle, photosynthesis takes up CO2. Respiration, decomposition and burning return CO2 to the air.

cards.p: Nitrogen-fixing bacteria such as Rhizobium turn N2 from the air into ammonia. Nitrification turns ammonia into nitrate, and denitrification turns nitrate back into N2. The phosphorus cycle has no gas stage.

text-anchor='middle'>dead organisms, waste → decomposers</text></svg>
cards.key: Decomposers turn the nitrogen in dead organisms into ammonia. This is called ammonification. Plants take up nitrogen mostly as nitrate. Phosphorus moves from rocks into the soil, and from there into living things.

cards.p: When fossil fuels burn, SO2 and nitrogen oxides are released into the air. These gases combine with moisture to form acids, and acid rain forms. Acid rain harms lakes, soil and forests, and it wears away marble.

cards.key: Normal rain is also slightly acidic (pH ≈ 5.6), but acid rain has a lower pH. Waste, fertilizers and pesticides also pollute water and soil.

once.soru: What is the main source of acid rain?

secenekler.neden: The SO₂ and nitrogen oxides released when coal and oil burn combine with moisture to form acids.
Ozone thinning is about UV rays, not acid.
Photosynthesis takes up CO₂. It does not produce acid.

cards.h: The greenhouse effect, climate and ozone
cards.p: The greenhouse effect is a natural process. CO2, methane and water vapor trap heat. When these gases increase, climate change begins. Ozone thinning is a separate problem. CFC gases weaken the ozone layer that protects against UV rays.

(1987)</text><path d='M6 156 H314' stroke='var(--line)' stroke-width='1' fill='none'/></svg>
cards.key: Fossil fuels and deforestation increase greenhouse gases. Glaciers melt and sea level rises. Ozone thinning is not the cause of global warming.

once.soru: What would Earth be like with no greenhouse effect at all?

secenekler.neden: If the gases did not trap heat, Earth's average temperature would be about −18 °C.
Greenhouse gases trap heat. Without them, Earth would cool down.
The greenhouse effect is a natural process and is needed for life.

cards.p: The eutrophication you just saw is started by the nitrogen and phosphorus in fertilizer. When plant cover disappears, soil is carried away by water and wind. This is called erosion. Habitat loss and overhunting reduce biodiversity.

cards.key: Invasive species also reduce biodiversity. They spread quickly because they have no natural enemies in their new home. The lionfish in the Mediterranean is an example.

cards.p: Species that naturally live only in one particular region are called endemic species. If an endemic species dies out in that region, it is gone from the world. About 80% of the plant species in Madagascar are endemic. Lemurs also live only on this island.

cards.key: Islands and high mountains isolate species, so they have many endemic species. The wild ancestors of wheat and chickpeas live in the Fertile Crescent.

once.soru: Galápagos giant tortoises live only on those islands. What are such species called?

secenekler.neden: An endemic species naturally lives only in one particular region.
An invasive species arrives in a new place and spreads quickly.
Pioneer species are the first to settle in a bare area.

cards.p: Sustainability means meeting today's needs without using up the options of future generations. The ecological footprint is the productive area needed for the resources we use and the waste we make. A smaller footprint is better.

cards.key: The main solutions are recycling, renewable energy, public transport, protected areas and international agreements.

once.soru: Which of these shrinks the ecological footprint?

secenekler.neden: Public transport cuts fuel use and emissions per person.
The more we consume, the bigger the ecological footprint.
The more waste there is, the bigger the ecological footprint.

cards.p: Waste management starts with preventing waste. We need to consume less and reuse things. The waste that remains is sorted at the source and goes to recycling, compost or the battery bin. A landfill is the last option.

cards.key: The right order is prevent, reuse and recycle. Burying is the last resort.

once.soru: What is the first choice in waste management?

secenekler.neden: The best waste is the waste that never forms.
Recycling is good, but it comes after preventing waste.
Burying waste is the last resort.

cards.p:
• An ecosystem is made of living things and the nonliving surroundings.
• Energy flows in one direction, and only about 10% passes to each level.
• Water, carbon, nitrogen and phosphorus move in cycles.
• Poisons build up going up the food chain.
• The answer to pollution, climate change and habitat loss is sustainability.

quiz.q: Put in order how a nitrogen atom moves from the air to a plant and back to the soil.
quiz.e: Bacteria fix N₂ into ammonia, and nitrifying bacteria turn ammonia into nitrate. The plant takes up nitrate with its roots and builds it into its proteins. When the plant dies, decomposers turn the nitrogen back into ammonia. This is called ammonification.

quiz.q: In a food chain, the producers store 50,000 kJ of energy. By the 10% rule, about how many kJ reach the secondary consumers?
quiz.e: 50,000 × 0.1 = 5,000 kJ passes to the primary consumers. Then 5,000 × 0.1 = 500 kJ passes to the secondary consumers.

quiz.q: Match each environmental problem with its main cause.
ciftler: SO₂ and NOₓ released into the air
quiz.e: SO₂ and nitrogen oxides form acids with moisture and cause acid rain. CFCs thin the ozone layer. Nitrogen and phosphorus from fertilizer cause eutrophication, rising greenhouse gases cause climate change and loss of plant cover causes erosion.

quiz.q: Which of the following statements is true?
o: An energy pyramid is never inverted.
Ozone thinning is the main cause of global warming.
Like matter, energy cycles through an ecosystem.
Scavengers such as vultures are decomposers.
quiz.e: Energy is lost as heat at every level. So the energy of a higher level can never be greater than that of the level below. The other options are common misconceptions.
y: Ozone thinning leads to more UV rays. The main cause of global warming is greenhouse gases.
Matter cycles, but energy flows in one direction and is lost as heat at every level.
A vulture is a consumer that tears up and eats carcasses. The decomposers are bacteria and fungi.
